principle: Searches the DATA rather than my memory of what a Pokémon fan knows. Memory finds the famous patterns and misses the odd ones.
proposesOnly: Candidate themes are proposed and never adopted. Deciding a group belongs together is taste, and taste goes in a file a person signs.

finds.headline: Ken Sugimori drew Ampharos exactly once
finds.hook: Ken Sugimori has 729 cards. Exactly one is a Ampharos.
finds.basis: artist field + count of that Pokémon in their output
finds.why: A single card carrying a fact nobody would guess and anybody can check.

finds.headline: Alakazam disappeared for 10 years
finds.hook: Alakazam was printed in 2009, then not again until 2019.
finds.basis: every print year for that Pokémon in our catalogue
finds.why: A gap in the data is a question waiting for somebody who knows the answer — which is exactly the kind of post that gets replies.

finds.headline: 11 Pokémon share the "-eon" ending
finds.basis: name pattern across the catalogue
finds.why: Proposed, not adopted: Charmeleon, Flareon, Jolteon, Umbreon, Kecleon, Empoleon, Lumineon, Finneon, Leafeon, Sylveon. Whether that is a THEME or a coincidence of Japanese naming is a judgment, and judgments go in data/themes.json where somebody can argue with them.
